metadata.note: The West Jersey system of South Jersey - the Millville, Cape May, Newfield - Atlantic City, Bridgeton, Elmer - Salem, Salem, Quinton, Penns Grove, Anglesea/Wildwood, Longport and Medford lines - built from research/branches/west_jersey_and_seashore_railroad.txt (researched 2026-10-20), drawing only its drawable: spans. One feature per drawable span and operator; features for the same corridor share identical geometry. Rule 4 splits: Millville and Glassboro / Cape May and Millville / Salem Railroad -> West Jersey 1868-69; West Jersey and West Jersey and Atlantic -> West Jersey and Seashore at the 4 May 1896 consolidation; Delaware River RR -> WJ&S 30 Apr 1900; Anglesea RR -> West Jersey 23 May 1888; WJ&S -> Pennsylvania-Reading Seashore Lines 15 Jul 1933 on the lines that kept passengers (Millville, Bridgeton, Salem, Penns Grove). NOT split: Swedesboro RR (leased before opening, 1869), Woodstown and Swedesboro (leased on opening, 1883), Alloway and Quinton (West Jersey-worked from opening, 1891), the 1879 Delaware Shore -> Delaware River RR reincorporation (same line, one feature), and the 1 Jul 1930 PRR lease (see not_yet_sourced). Segments end the year before the next operator's first year (the drawable spans), so no corridor is drawn twice in one year. NOT IN THIS LAYER: the Camden - Haddonfield - Atlantic City main line and the Delair Bridge / Bridge Line (report blocks 1-3) - drawn today in pennsylvania_railroad_system.geojson (prr-prsl-atlantic-city) and nj_transit_rail.geojson (njt-1), which open dataset PR #108 edits; drawing them here would double-draw. The Cape May County beach lines and Somers Point branch (block 37) are in ocean_city_railroad.geojson; the Camden and Atlantic / PM&M years of the Longport and Medford lines (block 38) belong to PR #108.

not_yet_sourced: THE 1 JULY 1930 PRR LEASE: the PRR formally leased the WJ&S from 1 Jul 1930 (Coverdale & Colpitts 1946 p.187 via Wikipedia). CLAUDE.md Rule 4 counts a lease as an operator change, but no source describes any change in how the trains were run in 1930, and ocean_city_railroad.geojson keeps its WJ&S features through 1933. By decision for this PR the WJ&S features here run through 1932 unsplit; if the project adopts the split, every wjs-* feature still running in 1930 (millville-line, millville-cape-may, newfield-atlantic-city, bridgeton-branch, salem-branch, penns-grove-branch) should split at 1930 into WJ&S 1896-1929 and Pennsylvania Railroad 1930-1932 (1930-1931 for Newfield), together with the wjs-* features in ocean_city_railroad.geojson.

[OPEN] ends - last CONFIRMED years, not known ends: wjs-elmer-branch 1928 (via the Quinton mixed train); wjs-anglesea-branch and wjs-wildwood-crest-extension 1921 (Five Mile Beach Weekly Journal 3 Jun 1921); wjs-atlantic-city-longport 1897 (Fowler 1897 company timetable). Do not extend without evidence.

wjs-millville-cape-may end: no dated last WJ&S passenger train. Drawn to 1932 on the Coverdale & Colpitts 'abandoned ... in favor of the former Cape May Railroad route' after the 1933 PRSL consolidation; sjrail's 26 Feb 1949 'last mail train' over the WJ&S line conflicts with a 1933 abandonment.

Cape May and Millville completion: Aug 1863 (C&M article) vs 1867 (WJ&S article); rail to Cape Island confirmed by 11 Jun 1866. The 1863-1865 railhead is unproven; the whole line is drawn from 1863. Lease 1 Jun 1868 vs 1869.
Salem Railroad lease: 1 Jan 1868 (Coverdale & Colpitts) vs June 1868 (Wilson 1899).

West Jersey and Atlantic operator 1880-1895: own board, but 'ultimately leased to the WJ' (date not given) and trains advertised 'Via West Jersey Railroad' in 1895. If the West Jersey worked it, recolour wja-newfield-atlantic-city (and wja-somers-point-branch in ocean_city_railroad.geojson) to the West Jersey.
Delaware River RR operator 1876-1900: newspaper timetable headings outlived the company by five years and do not prove who crewed the trains.
Millville and Glassboro operator after the West Jersey reached Glassboro in Apr 1861: not established.
Anglesea RR own-name operation 1883-1887: implied by incorporation and receivership, not confirmed by a timetable. Wildwood Crest extension opening date not found (drawn from Fowler's 1907t).
Woodstown and Swedesboro opening: 1883 (W&S article; Fowler) vs 'February 23, 1873' (WJ&S article, treated as an error).
Millville line last train 5 Feb 1971 vs 5 Mar 1971; end of electric service 24 Sep vs 8 Sep 1949 - same years.
Headways: none measured except the counts noted per segment; every headway_min is an estimate. avg_speed_kmh is an estimate throughout.
